Subject: Help: model output truncates mid-sentence during batch runs

Hi Evelyn / Redwood support,

We're seeing an intermittent truncation problem from the Redwood API across several sessions in the last three days. Some responses are cut off mid-sentence — not a JSON parse error, just the generated text ending abruptly. It happened on Nov 12, 13 and 14 during concurrent runs (100 req/s for short prompts).

I attached a small snippet (acme_truncated_snippet.txt) with the prompt, a sample truncated output, and a timestamp. We don't currently see an HTTP 5xx; the request returns 200 but the body stops after ~120 tokens.

Environment:
- SDK: redwood-js 0.9.2
- Model: llama-v2-13b-quant (hosted)
- Region: us-west1

Can you confirm if this looks like a server-side truncation or something on our end? We captured request timestamps and can share request-ids if that helps. This is affecting a small percent of in-production customer responses, so would like to understand scope.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Garcia
Engineering Manager, Acme Retail

Hi Elena — I attempted to reproduce based on the prompt and concurrency description you shared. Summary of steps and findings:

1) Ran 200 short-prompt requests across 4 hosts (us-west1) with temperatures 0.0–0.8 and max_tokens=256 to mirror your workload.
2) Observed no instances of abrupt truncation; all responses terminated with expected stop tokens or reached the token limit.
3) Inspected server logs for the window you indicated and did not find correlated 5xx or runtime exceptions for the app IDs associated with your account.

I attached a short excerpt of our repro attempt logs (redwood_repro_log_excerpt.txt). Notable observations:
- No kernel OOMs or GRPC stream resets in the timeframe we tested.
- A small number of client-side timeouts were observed across unrelated customers, but not with the same request-ids as yours.

Possible explanations:
- Client-side socket close or truncated reading of the response body (SDK/network) before the stream completed.
- Intermittent proxy/loadbalancer interaction at your side under sustained high concurrency.

Next steps:
- If you can provide 3 exact request-ids (from your logs) when you saw truncation, we'll fetch server traces for those ids.
- If that's not possible, we recommend running a short repro while we tail logs together (we can join a Zoom and watch request-ids appear).

If you prefer we open a formal INF ticket, I've created INF-2026 and linked it below; I've set tentative priority P2 until we can reproduce.

Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Help: model output truncates mid-sentence during batch runs — post-triage summary

Hi Elena — thanks for sharing the request-id and for scheduling the session. Quick post-triage update following our repro session and log review: 

- We were unable to reproduce truncation on Redwood servers during the session while generating at the concurrency levels you used. Server-side traces for request ACME-REQ-20261113-8891 show a complete token stream delivered by the runtime (server-side status: 200 OK).
- SRE inspected connection logs and there’s evidence that the connection between your proxy and our edge occasionally resets during brief spikes; these resets correlate with the time windows you originally reported.
- No runtime exceptions, OOMs, or model-side truncation were found on Redwood's hosts.

Resolution/ask:
- Our finding: no server-side truncation was observed; the evidence points to intermittent networking/proxy behavior on your side that can cause the client to stop reading the stream prematurely.
- Please confirm whether your proxy enforces any per-connection timeouts or body-size limits at high concurrency, and if possible, disable or raise them for a short window to validate.
- We will keep INF-2026 open for two more weeks to monitor; if you capture any additional request-ids that show truncation, please forward them and we'll pull full traces immediately.

I've added the session notes to INF-2026 (link below). If you'd like a formal postmortem, we can draft a short doc describing the evidence and recommended mitigations.

Thanks again for working through this — happy to keep the session open and retest with any config changes on your side.

—Evelyn
